rows.title: Entrance: Early Discoveries
rows.description: Curie's Ghost appears from the past!

monster.name: Curie's Ghost
monster.defeatMessage: The Ghost honors your knowledge of radioactivity!

questions.question: Who discovered radioactivity?
The scientist who discovered radioactivity (last name):

rows.explanation: He found it accidentally while studying uranium salts. Becquerel noticed that these materials could expose photographic plates even without sunlight, which led him to realize that the energy was coming from the uranium itself—this phenomenon is what we now call radioactivity.

rows.title: Corridor: Atomic Structure
rows.description: Rutherford's Robot guards this path!

monster.name: Rutherford's Robot
monster.defeatMessage: The Robot acknowledges your atomic wisdom!

questions.question: What did Ernest Rutherford's gold foil experiment discover?
The center of an atom:

rows.explanation: Rutherford's experiment showed that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus, with most of the atom being empty space.

rows.title: Chamber: Nuclear Fission
rows.description: The Fission Fiend blocks your way!

monster.name: Fission Fiend
monster.defeatMessage: The Fission Fiend splits apart in defeat!

questions.question: When was nuclear fission first discovered?
Splitting of an atomic nucleus:

rows.explanation: Nuclear fission was discovered in 1938 by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann, with theoretical explanation by Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch.

rows.title: Hallway: First Reactor
rows.description: Reactor Rex roars with power!

monster.name: Reactor Rex
monster.defeatMessage: Reactor Rex powers down!

questions.question: Where was the first controlled nuclear chain reaction achieved?
Italian physicist who led the first reactor (last name):

rows.explanation: The first controlled nuclear chain reaction was achieved on December 2, 1942, at the University of Chicago under the direction of Enrico Fermi.

rows.title: Final Chamber: Modern Era
rows.description: The Modern Menace challenges you!

monster.name: Modern Menace
monster.defeatMessage: The Modern Menace fades into history!

questions.question: What organization promotes the peaceful use of nuclear energy?
UN agency for atomic energy (abbreviation):

rows.explanation: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) promotes the peaceful use of nuclear energy and works to prevent nuclear weapons proliferation.

rows.title: Entrance: What is Radiation?
rows.description: A Proton Prowler guards the entrance!

monster.name: Proton Prowler
monster.defeatMessage: The Proton Prowler has been atomized!

questions.question: What particle in an atom determines which element it is?
Positively charged particles in the nucleus:

rows.explanation: The number of protons (atomic number) determines the element. Carbon always has 6 protons, oxygen has 8, uranium has 92.

rows.title: Corridor: Isotopes
rows.description: The Isotope Imp blocks your path!

monster.name: Isotope Imp
monster.defeatMessage: The Isotope Imp has decayed away!

questions.question: What are isotopes?
options: Atoms with different numbers of protons
Atoms with different numbers of neutrons
Atoms with different numbers of electrons

questions.question: Same element, different mass versions:

rows.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same protons) with different numbers of neutrons. Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 are both carbon but have different neutron counts.

rows.title: Chamber: Natural Radiation
rows.description: A Cosmic Crawler descends from above!

monster.name: Cosmic Crawler
monster.defeatMessage: The Cosmic Crawler returns to space!

questions.question: Which of these is a natural source of radiation?
options: Cosmic rays from space and radon gas

questions.question: Radioactive gas found in some homes:

rows.explanation: Natural radiation comes from cosmic rays, radon gas, radioactive materials in the Earth's crust, and even from food (like bananas containing potassium-40).

rows.title: Hallway: Radiation Types
rows.description: The Alpha Assassin attacks!

monster.name: Alpha Assassin
monster.defeatMessage: The Alpha Assassin has been blocked!

questions.question: Which type of radiation can be stopped by a sheet of paper?
Most penetrating type of radiation:
questions.hint: Requires thick lead or concrete to block

rows.explanation: Alpha particles are the least penetrating form of radiation and can be stopped by a sheet of paper or even the outer layer of skin.

rows.title: Final Chamber: Half-Life
rows.description: The Half-Life Hunter stands in your way!

monster.name: Half-Life Hunter
monster.defeatMessage: The Half-Life Hunter has finally decayed!

questions.question: Carbon-14 is used in carbon dating. Why does it work?
options: C-14 decays at a predictable rate (half-life)

questions.question: Time for half of radioactive atoms to decay:

rows.explanation: Carbon-14 is radioactive and decays at a predictable rate (half-life of 5,730 years). By measuring how much C-14 remains, we can determine how long ago an organism died.

rows.title: Entrance: Reactor Basics
rows.description: A Uranium Urchin emerges from the fuel rods!

monster.name: Uranium Urchin
monster.defeatMessage: The Uranium Urchin goes subcritical!

questions.question: What is the primary fuel used in most nuclear reactors?
Main element used as reactor fuel:

rows.explanation: Uranium-235 is the primary fissile isotope used in most nuclear reactors. It can sustain a nuclear chain reaction.

rows.title: Corridor: Chain Reaction
rows.description: The Chain Chomper attacks!

monster.name: Chain Chomper
monster.defeatMessage: The Chain Chomper's reaction is controlled!

questions.question: What happens when a uranium-235 nucleus splits?
Self-sustaining nuclear process:

rows.explanation: When U-235 splits (fission), it releases energy and 2-3 neutrons. These neutrons can then cause other U-235 nuclei to split, creating a chain reaction.

rows.title: Chamber: Reactor Types
rows.description: The Pressure Python coils around the room!

monster.name: Pressure Python
monster.defeatMessage: The Pressure Python releases its steam!

questions.question: What is the most common type of nuclear reactor worldwide?
Most common reactor type (abbreviation):

rows.explanation: Pressurized Water Reactors (PWRs) are the most common type, accounting for about two-thirds of all nuclear reactors worldwide.

rows.title: Hallway: Cooling Systems
rows.description: A Coolant Crawler emerges from the pipes!

monster.name: Coolant Crawler
monster.defeatMessage: The Coolant Crawler evaporates!

questions.question: Why do nuclear reactors need cooling systems?
options: To prevent the fuel from freezing
To remove heat generated by fission
Both to remove heat and to create steam

questions.question: Liquid used to remove heat from reactor:

rows.explanation: Cooling systems remove the immense heat generated by nuclear fission and transfer it to create steam that drives turbines to generate electricity.

rows.title: Chamber: Fuel Cycle
rows.description: The Fuel Fiend blocks your path!

monster.name: Fuel Fiend
monster.defeatMessage: The Fuel Fiend is spent!

questions.question: What percentage of uranium-235 is typically found in reactor fuel?
Process of increasing U-235 concentration:

rows.explanation: Reactor fuel is typically enriched to 3-5% U-235. Natural uranium contains only 0.7% U-235, while weapons-grade requires 90%+ enrichment.

rows.title: Final Chamber: Reactor Safety
rows.description: The Safety Sergeant stands guard!

monster.name: Safety Sergeant
monster.defeatMessage: The Safety Sergeant stands down!

questions.question: What is the purpose of a reactor's emergency core cooling system?
options: To cool the reactor core in emergency situations

questions.question: Abbreviation for Emergency Core Cooling System:

rows.explanation: Emergency core cooling systems are designed to inject cooling water into the reactor core if normal cooling is lost, preventing core damage.

rows.title: Entrance: Reactor Basics
rows.description: A Control Creeper blocks your path!

monster.name: Control Creeper
monster.defeatMessage: The Control Creeper's chain reaction has been stopped!

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of control rods in a nuclear reactor?
options: To absorb neutrons and control the reaction rate

questions.question: Control rods absorb these particles to slow reactions:

rows.explanation: Control rods are made of materials that absorb neutrons. By inserting or withdrawing them, operators can control the rate of the nuclear chain reaction.

rows.title: Corridor: Emergency Systems
rows.description: The Containment Beast guards this passage!

monster.name: Containment Beast
monster.defeatMessage: The Containment Beast has been safely contained!

questions.question: What is the purpose of a containment building?
options: To contain radioactive materials in case of an accident

questions.question: The thick concrete structure around a reactor:

rows.explanation: Containment buildings are massive structures designed to prevent the release of radioactive materials even in the event of a severe accident.

rows.title: Chamber: Radiation Protection
rows.description: A Radiation Phantom haunts this chamber!

monster.name: Radiation Phantom
monster.defeatMessage: The Radiation Phantom fades away harmlessly!

questions.question: What are the three principles of radiation protection?
Material that blocks radiation:
Which material is commonly used for radiation shielding?

rows.explanation: The three principles of radiation protection are: minimize time exposed, maximize distance from source, and use shielding materials.

rows.title: Final Chamber: Emergency Response
rows.description: The Emergency Golem awaits your challenge!

monster.name: Emergency Golem
monster.defeatMessage: The Emergency Golem has been neutralized!

questions.question: What is the primary goal of emergency response at a nuclear facility?
options: To protect public health and safety
To shut down the reactor permanently

questions.question: International agency that sets nuclear safety standards:

rows.explanation: Emergency response prioritizes protecting public health and safety through coordinated, measured responses based on the situation.
